catalog_quote: 6.2.3. Waigeo Ma'ya (all dialects) The Waigeo dialects of Ma'ya are Kawe, Wauyai and Laganyan (see Chapter II). While Laganyan has lexical tone, Kawe and Wauyai do not. In terms of lexical stress and vowel distribution, on the other hand, there is not much difference between the three dialects. ... In the Waigeo dialects, if such words [words that have penultimate stress] have the same vowel in penultimate and final syllables, and end in an open syllable, the final syllable vowel is apocopated when the word appears in sentence-medial context. ... [6.4.3] I. If a polysyllabic word has a vowel other than /a/ in the penultimate syllable, it can only have penultimate stress. Otherwise, stress is contrastive, either on the penultimate or on the final syllable. ... [ch. sources.citation: Arnold, Laura. 2026. Sketch grammars of Wauyai Maˈya and Batta: Two undocumented Austronesian languages of Raja Ampat, northwest New Guinea. Language Documentation & Conservation 20: 1-51. hdl.handle.net/10125/74842
sources.quote: "As first noted by Remijsen (2001a; 2001b), Wauyai also has an orthogonal system of contrastive stress: in the majority of words, either the penultimate or final syllable of a word bears stress. Perceptual correlates of stress are a greater intensity, longer vowel duration, and falling pitch. Words with penultimate stress cannot bear Rise tone." Minimal pairs: ˈmɐnɐ³ 'light (weight)' vs mɐˈnɐ³ 'animal fat' vs mɐˈnɐ¹² 'mucus'; ˈɐnɐ 'thing'. sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Ma'ya has three lexically contrastive tonemes (High, Rise, Fall); accounts of the Misool, Salawati and Laganyan dialect tone systems and their diachrony (Rise most variable; Misool push-chain shift of Fall; Laganyan loses the Fall/Rise contrast in one context and has a boundary tone surfacing with voiced codas). For Wauyai itself it classes the dialect as lacking lexical tone (per Arnold 2025 fn.12, 2026 p.5) - the analysis Arnold 2026 overturns.

tone.summary: Ma'ya: 3 tonemes H, Rise, Fall (Remijsen); Wauyai analysed as atonal here, contra Arnold 2026.

For Wauyai itself it classes the dialect as lacking lexical tone (per Arnold 2025 fn.12, 2026 p.5) - the analysis Arnold 2026 overturns.
